Slinger Francisco, who performed as the Mighty Sparrow, died on Sunday surrounded by family in New York

Slinger Francisco, known on stage as the Mighty Sparrow and dubbed the “calypso king of the world”, has died aged 91.

Francisco, who got his breakthrough in calypso music with his 1956 hit song Jean and Dinah, died peacefully surrounded by his family in New York on Sunday, his family said in a statement.

Hurricane Nolo was moving away from the Hawaiian islands on Sunday, but the threat of heavy rain, flash flooding and strong winds persisted in areas of the island chain still recovering from previous storms.

guardian.description:
President’s ‘hard, drastic and necessary measure’, likely to attract widespread public support, polls suggest

The Brazilian president, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, has signed an order banning fixed-odds sports betting just over a week before the first round of the presidential election, in a move he said was designed to tackle the pervasive problem of families falling into debt.

The decision ends the operation, offering, intermediation and advertising of betting.

South Korea has demanded an apology from North Korea over a landmine blast that injured three soldiers, saying they were hurt by North Korean mines on the southern side of the border.

guardian.description:
Detained anti-human trafficking campaigners include Tran Hiep, a Vietnamese Australian, not heard from since 18 September

Vietnamese authorities have detained three activists, including a Norwegian and an Australian, on what have been described as “fabricated” charges.

The Vietnamese government said the three confessed to being members of Viet Tan – a pro-democracy organisation – which it describes as a terrorist group.

guardian.title: Trump asked Xi Jinping if China would like to buy US weapons, American ambassador says

David Perdue’s remarks come after a Taiwanese minister spoke of the ‘severe’ military threat posed by Beijing to the self-ruled island

Donald Trump offered to sell weapons to China while hosting its leader, Xi Jinping, last week, the US ambassador to China said on Sunday.

David Perdue told Fox News on Sunday: “President Trump continues to say, hey, we sell arms to other people around the world. He actually asked President Xi, would he like to buy some at one point.”

rfi.title: US Supreme Court lifts limits on third-country deportations
rfi.description: The US Supreme Court on Tuesday lifted restrictions on the deportations of immigrants to countries that are not their own, while agreeing to hear the issue on its merits in December.

rfi.title: Mali army and Russian fighters accused of killing dozens of civilians
rfi.description: Mali’s armed forces and Russian Wagner Group personnel committed war crimes including killings and torture of civilians during joint operations between 2023 and 2025, Amnesty International has said in a new report documenting abuses across several regions of the country.

rfi.title: Heatwaves and wildfires drive extreme ozone pollution worldwide
rfi.description: Heatwaves, wildfires and human-caused emissions exposed a third of the world’s population to extremely high ozone pollution in 2026, with Asia worst hit and wildfire smoke crossing oceans, an EU report said on Wednesday.

rfi.title: Le Pen ally Bardella sues over antisemitism claims, alleges 'total war'
rfi.description: Jordan Bardella, a key ally of French far-right presidential frontrunner Marine Le Pen, on Tuesday said allegations he made antisemitic comments in 2013 marked part of a "total war" against their National Rally party ahead of the 2027 polls. Backed by fellow party members, Bardella announced that he had filed a complaint for defamation.

rfi.title: French PM warns against student violence as public sector strike kicks off
rfi.description: French Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu has warned against an escalation of the demonstrations in secondary schools, which have broken out ahead of a nationwide strike by public-sector workers. More than 100 pupils were arrested on Monday during violent clashes with police. It comes amid mounting anger over the national budget, which is due to be unveiled on Thursday.

rfi.title: French public sector workers strike over pay freeze ahead of 2027 budget
rfi.description: Teachers, healthcare workers, local government staff, tax officials and firefighters in France are on strike Tuesday to pressure the government ahead of the 2027 budget debates which could see public sector salaries frozen for a fourth straight year.

rfi.title: Burkina Faso, Mali and Niger launch Tafouk TV channel to push their own narrative
rfi.description: Burkina Faso, Mali and Niger are stepping up their joint media push with Tafouk TV, a new television channel aimed at challenging Western coverage and promoting the three military-led Sahel states’ own account of events.

rfi.title: French prosecutors seek 'severe' punishment for ex-minister Dati in graft case
rfi.description: France prosecutors on Monday sought two years with an electronic tag and a five-year ban on public office for ex-culture minister Rachida Dati in a trial on corruption charges linked to dealings with the Renault-Nissan group. Her lawyers have slammed the severity of the recommendations which will be announced in January next year.

rfi.title: US has 'alienated' Sudan's army in 'complex war' analyst tells RFI
rfi.description: Sudan's army chief Abdel Fattah al-Burhan has vowed to push on with his fight against the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces, despite a US visa snub to attend the UN General Assembly and mounting pressure for a ceasefire. RFI spoke to a Sudanese researcher about why such a step was taken and how far the stand-off could go.

rfi.title: Egypt, Senegal and Ghana face pressure to relaunch drive for 2027 AFCON
rfi.description: Continental powerhouses Egypt, Ghana and Senegal will attempt to get their 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifying campaigns back on track on Tuesday after opening round setbacks last week.

rfi.title: Old hand Olise rewards Zidane's fresh blood adventure in Belgium
rfi.description: Michael Olise came off the substitutes bench on Monday night to score a sensational late goal for France against Belgium to give new boss Zinedine Zidane his second victory in two matches.

rfi.title: French church abuse victims praise Pope Leo for 'extraordinary' empathy
rfi.description: French victims of clerical abuse called their meeting with Pope Leo XIV on Sunday "extraordinary", praising him for listening deeply to their experiences. The Pope said he was committed to preventing further harm.

rfi.title: Houthi attacks put Turkey’s new Saudi defence pact to the test
rfi.description: Attacks by Yemen's Houthi rebels on Saudi Arabia are putting Turkey's new defence pact with the kingdom to its first major test – forcing Ankara to weigh support for its ally against the risk of being drawn deeper into the conflict.

rfi.title: French women face growing obstacles to abortion despite constitutional right
rfi.description: The right to terminate a pregnancy was formally enshrined in the French Constitution in 2024, but women are finding it harder to gain access due to geographical inequalities and lack of information but also rising prejudice, France's family planning movement has said.

rfi.title: Gisèle Pelicot's daughter launches awareness campaign on chemical submission
rfi.description: An association founded by the daughter of Gisèle Pelicot, who was drugged by her ex-husband and raped by him and dozens of other men, has launched an awareness campaign on chemical submission.

rfi.title: Iranian lawyer Nasrin Sotoudeh wins 2026 Vaclav Havel human rights prize
rfi.description: Iranian human rights lawyer Nasrin Sotoudeh was awarded the Council of Europe’s Vaclav Havel Human Rights Prize on Monday for her work defending activists, journalists, minorities and opponents of the death penalty.

rfi.title: 'We’re short of everything' say striking French firefighters
rfi.description: French firefighters, who have been on strike since 8 September, set up camp at the foot of the Eiffel Tower in Paris on Sunday to draw the government’s attention to a lack of resources following a scorching summer marked by a surge in wildfires. They are also due to join a public-sector strike planned across France on Tuesday.

rfi.title: Ethiopia accuses Sudan, Eritrea of backing Tigray forces as fighting escalates
rfi.description: Addis Ababa has accused Sudan and Eritrea of backing armed groups fighting its federal forces in the north, claims Khartoum has rejected as renewed clashes raise fears of a return to full-scale conflict.

euronews.title: No, Macron isn't planning to trigger a war with Russia to stay in power
euronews.description: Allegations are circulating online that Macron will put France at war with Russia to postpone elections and stay in power as his second consecutive term comes to an end. However, the country's constitution makes this unfeasible in many ways.

euronews.title: Deadly Russian attacks on Ukraine kill at least four and hit Kyiv power supply
euronews.description: Ensuring energy supply is critical as the cold winter months approach. Russian strikes on the sector last year cut light and heating as temperatures plunged to as low as -20C.

euronews.title: Mental health under scrutiny: Spain lags Europe in psychologists, pay or wait
euronews.description: With six clinical psychologists per 100,000 people, against nearly 18 in Europe, regular therapy in Spain is out of reach for many; the alternative is costly private care.

euronews.title: Flooding and destruction as Hurricane Polo hits Mexico
euronews.description: Hurricane Polo has caused flooding and damage in parts of Mexico, with aerial footage showing inundated streets and ground images showing damaged roofs, fallen branches and residents clearing debris.

euronews.title: Belgian minister Theo Francken warns Europe: 'Everything has to go faster' on defence
euronews.description: Belgian Defence Minister Theo Francken told the Euronews Defence Summit in Brussels that Europe faces a “dark winter” of Russian hybrid attacks and urgently needs stronger air defences, describing Russia as the biggest threat to Belgium’s security.

euronews.title: World's tallest wind turbine reaches final height in Germany's former coal mining region
euronews.description: Winds are stronger at higher altitudes, allowing for twice as much energy to be produced.

euronews.title: Flydubai plane traveling to Israel diverted to Saudi Arabia after alleged dispute between pilots
euronews.description: FlyDubai flight FZ1073 transmitted an emergency alert shortly after take-off, according to publicly available flight tracking information.

euronews.title: Unlike the EU, Trump's new AI pact lets tech companies police themselves
euronews.description: Tech bosses from Nvidia, OpenAI and Anthropic signed a White House pledge on Tuesday to keep their AI in check, with no legal force behind it. In the EU, the same companies face fines of up to 3% of global turnover if they break the rules.

euronews.title: Rehabilitated green sea turtle Jurassic returns to Atlantic
euronews.description: Jurassic, a 215-pound adult male green sea turtle, has been released back into the Atlantic Ocean after rehabilitation in Florida, equipped with a satellite tracker to monitor his movements.

euronews.title: Russia is ‘testing how far it can go' before the EU reacts, says Tsikhanouskaya
euronews.description: Belarusian opposition leader Sviatlana Tsikhanouskaya believes change in Russia could begin with change in Belarus, arguing that her country’s opposition movement is “more consolidated” than its Russian counterpart.

euronews.title: Gene therapy: The breakthrough that inspired Spider-Man | Euronews Tech Talks
euronews.description: Although an inspiration for science fiction movies, gene therapy is real. Here is how it works and what could be improved about it.

euronews.title: The birth of a painting: Artist Merike Estna on creating in public at the Venice Biennale
euronews.description: Estonia artist Merike Estna did something extremely unusual for the Venice Biennale, even by its own standards. Over the past five months, she created paintings live in front of daily visitors. The result is 22 canvases which explore the themes of motherhood and feminism.

euronews.title: Exclusive: Germany shields parts of Deutsche Börse from EU oversight
euronews.description: The EU is negotiating a reform in Brussels to better integrate its capital markets. Germany has secured an exemption for major European operator Deutsche Börse’s domestically focused trading venues from centralised supervision, leaving a key part of the system under regional control.

euronews.title: Europe's security and defence in focus amid escalating hybrid threats
euronews.description: Good morning. This is Mared Gwyn in Brussels, where Euronews’ Defence and Space Summit is just about to get underway – more on that below. Also in this edition: an exclusive interview with the head of President Zelenskyy’s office, Kyrylo Budanov.

euronews.title: Underground fire: Blaze in German lignite mine cannot be extinguished
euronews.description: Sparked by a forest fire, hardly any flames are visible above ground, yet underground it still smoulders on a former lignite site in Thuringia and could burn for years.

euronews.title: Euronews Defence Summit: US ambassador warns 'Made in Europe' alienates NATO allies
euronews.description: NATO Secretary General, EU and top US officials join Euronews' Defence and Space Summit in Brussels on Wednesday as Europe seeks to strengthen its defence capabilities, respond to hybrid threats and develop a more integrated industrial base.

euronews.title: Fuel prices above two euros: Who will foot the biggest bill in Portugal?
euronews.description: From fishing to agriculture, and from freight to passenger transport, many sectors have felt the impact of sharp fuel price rises in Portugal since the war began in the Middle East.

euronews.title: Europe Today: NATO chief Mark Rutte joins Euronews' Defence and Space Summit in Brussels
euronews.description: Euronews hosts its biggest-ever news event, the Defence & Space Summit in Brussels, with NATO chief Mark Rutte among the guests. Meanwhile, Ukraine races to build interceptor drones against Russia's jet-powered strikes, and Estonia blames Russia for an arson attack on a defence firm.

lemonde.title: Jordan Bardella, une jeunesse au FN sous l’influence idéologique d’Alain Soral
lemonde.description: Accusé d’avoir produit des écrits antisémites lorsqu’il était jeune militant, ce qu’il conteste, le président du Rassemblement national a évolué dans un environnement où l’influence d’Alain Soral était manifeste. Brièvement membre du Front national, le polémiste antisémite est resté dans les années 2010 une référence populaire et, pour certains, une boussole idéologique.

lemonde.title: L’inflation sur un an atteint 3 %, selon les données provisoires de l’Insee
lemonde.description: Selon l’Insee, cette nouvelle augmentation de l’inflation s’explique par l’accélération de la hausse des prix de l’énergie (+ 21,2 % en septembre, contre + 16,7 %) et des produits frais (+ 9,9 %, contre + 5,9 % en août). La vague d’inflation s’explique principalement par le déclenchement de la guerre en Iran et le blocage du détroit d’Ormuz.

lemonde.title: Blocages des lycées : la mobilisation continue, Edouard Geffray juge les revendications « légitimes » tout en condamnant la violence
lemonde.description: L’Union syndicale lycéenne s’est dite prête à rencontrer le ministre de l’éducation nationale. Elle a aussi annoncé une « mobilisation commune » jeudi et mardi prochain avec l’Union étudiante, disant croire à « une convergence des luttes ».

lemonde.title: Le Gard et l’Hérault placés en vigilance rouge « pluie-inondation », Météo-France prévoit un épisode méditerranéen « remarquable », voire « exceptionnel »
lemonde.description: La Lozère et l’Ardèche sont placées en vigilance orange, tandis que les Bouches-du-Rhône seront classées au même niveau à partir de midi. Les établissements scolaires ont été fermés dans le Gard.

lemonde.title: « Les collègues toxiques restent en place » : quand les politiques de bien-être au travail occultent une organisation défaillante
lemonde.description: Les politiques pour la qualité de vie et les conditions de travail peuvent paradoxalement contribuer à la souffrance des salariés. C’est notamment le cas lorsqu’elles considèrent le stress et le mal-être comme un problème individuel.

lemonde.title: « Digger », d’Alejandro Gonzalez Iñarritu : Tom Cruise en vieillard misanthrope et obscène
lemonde.description: Le réalisateur mexicain livre une farce apocalyptique en même temps qu’une charge anti-MAGA d’une verte crudité.

lemonde.title: EN DIRECT, guerre en Ukraine :  la Russie est passée à des « frappes massives contre les infrastructures énergétiques », dénonce Kiev
lemonde.description: Les bombardements russes ont fait cinq morts et quatorze blessés. La principale cible a été le secteur énergétique de Kiev et de sa région.

lemonde.title: Présidentielle 2027 : Gabriel Attal critique le projet de réforme des retraites d’Edouard Philippe, jugeant qu’il s’agit de « mesures de soins palliatifs »
lemonde.description: La proposition d’Edouard Philippe, parvenir progressivement à un âge légal de départ à 65 ans avec 45 annuités de cotisation, c’est « la proposition Macron de 2022 », selon Gabriel Attal, qui propose, lui, une suppression de l’âge légal de départ.

lemonde.title: Adaptation de la France au changement climatique : le plan du ministère de la transition écologique soumis à l’arbitrage budgétaire de Matignon
lemonde.description: La ministre de la transition écologique, Monique Barbut, doit remettre le 30 septembre au premier ministre, Sébastien Lecornu, une feuille de route visant à accélérer la mise en œuvre du plan national d’adaptation au changement climatique.

lemonde.title: Piratage de Hugging Face : une ONG assigne OpenAI devant la justice pour infraction à la loi sur les cyberattaques
lemonde.description: Il s’agit de la première procédure connue contre une entreprise du secteur, en rapport avec les récents dérapages spontanés de l’intelligence artificielle dont ont fait état cet été OpenAI mais aussi Anthropic, Google et Meta.

lemonde.title: Au Royaume-Uni, Andy Burnham lance sa campagne pour 2029
lemonde.description: Dans son plan, esquissé mardi lors d’un discours au congrès travailliste, le premier ministre britannique a dit souhaiter revenir sur les politiques de privatisation engagées dans les années 1980 et sur les effets délétères du Brexit.

lemonde.title: Rakuten France : le site de vente en ligne cessera son activité à partir du 1ᵉʳ octobre
lemonde.description: Faute de repreneur, la plateforme annonce sur sa page d’accueil qu’à compter de cette date il ne sera plus possible d’effectuer d’achats ni de ventes. Confrontée à la concurrence, la « marketplace » n’a jamais réussi à enrayer le déclin de son activité. Quelque 180 salariés sont concernés.

lemonde.title: Le réchauffement de l’océan se poursuit « à un rythme alarmant », selon le programme européen Copernicus
lemonde.description: Alors qu’un phénomène El Niño d’ampleur s’installe dans le Pacifique, l’océan mondial subit les effets du réchauffement climatique. Le rythme de la montée des eaux a doublé au cours des deux dernières décennies.

lemonde.title: Chaussures André : « Quitter le “Titanic” sur un radeau de fortune n’aura pas suffi à sauver les anciennes gloires de l’empire Vivarte »
lemonde.description: Le tribunal des activités économiques de Paris a prononcé, le 9 septembre, la liquidation judiciaire d’Heritage 1896, la société qui exploitait depuis janvier les reliquats du chausseur, né en 1896 à Nancy, raconte Isabelle Chaperon, chroniqueuse au service Economie du « Monde ».

lemonde.title: Les géants de l’IA ne s’intéressent aux résultats mathématiques que pour afficher leur puissance
lemonde.description: Les maths ne se réduisent pas à une liste de sommets à conquérir, mais sont d’abord un art de comprendre, rappelle dans sa Carte blanche au « Monde », Etienne Ghys, regrettant que la discipline soit désormais envahie par les pouvoirs de l’argent.

lemonde.title: Appel à témoignages : vous avez moins de 30 ans et vous souffrez d’anxiété sociale ? Racontez-nous
lemonde.description: Depuis quelque temps, vous vivez avec une phobie sociale ? Cela vous handicape dans votre vie relationnelle ? Témoignez.

france24fr.title: Un vol Dubaï-Tel Aviv dérouté suite à une bagarre dans le cockpit
france24fr.description: Un vol Flydubai reliant Dubaï à Tel-Aviv a dû atterrir en urgence à Tabuk, en Arabie saoudite, après un « incident » en vol, tous les passagers étant sains et saufs. Des médias israéliens évoquent une altercation entre le pilote et le copilote, déclenchant le signal de détresse et l’intervention de chasseurs israéliens, mais les circonstances exactes restent à établir. Les précisions de Stéphane Amar depuis Jérusalem.

france24fr.title: France : l'inflation atteint 3 % sur un an en septembre, selon l'Insee
france24fr.description: La hausse des prix à la consommation s'est accéléré en septembre, atteignant 3 % sur un an. Elle est portée par la hausse des prix de l'énergie et des produits frais, selon une estimation provisoire publiée mercredi par l'Insee.

france24fr.title: Sur Reporterre : Attention aux labels et logos trompeurs
france24fr.description: Les labels écolos à gogo, c’est fini : l’Europe met un stop au greenwashing des marques. « Bien-être animal » pour les poulets : un logo qui prend les consommateurs pour des jambons. Explications avec Amélie Mougey, rédactrice en chef chez Reporterre

france24fr.title: Maroc : Fatima Ezzahra El Mansouri, de la mairie de Marrakech à la tête du gouvernement
france24fr.description: Elle dit vouloir "redonner espoir" aux jeunes. Fatima Ezzahra El Mansouri est devenue mardi la première femme cheffe de gouvernement au Maroc. Retour sur le parcours de cette avocate de formation de 50 ans, qui avait déjà été la première femme élue maire de Marrakech.

france24fr.title: France 24 en Irak : les dernières troupes de la coalition menée par les États-Unis quittent le pays
france24fr.description: Le retrait des dernières forces de la coalition internationale d’Irak marque la fin d’une présence militaire entamée en 2014. Pour les habitants, cette nouvelle étape doit permettre à l’Irak de retrouver sa souveraineté, après des années où les bases américaines et les factions armées pro-iraniennes ont contribué aux tensions. Bagdad prépare ses forces à assurer seules la défense du territoire, tout en faisant pression sur les groupes armés pour qu’ils désarment, s’intègrent aux institutions ou

france24fr.title: Cisjordanie occupée : face aux violences de colons, une rare condamnation israélienne
france24fr.description: En Cisjordanie, les violences de colons israéliens se poursuivent, avec plus de 1 600 attaques recensées depuis le début de l’année par l’ONU. À Jalud et Al-Mughayyir, des habitants palestiniens racontent avoir vu leurs maisons et leurs véhicules incendiés. Une rare condamnation est venue du président israélien Isaac Herzog après une attaque ayant également blessé des forces de sécurité israéliennes.

france24fr.title: Dette française : un nouveau record à 3 595 milliards d’euros
france24fr.description: 3 595 milliards et demi d’euros… Un chiffre à treize chiffres qui donne le vertige. C’est le montant de la dette française, publié ce matin par l’Insee. Un nouveau record, avec près de 60 milliards d’euros supplémentaires en seulement trois mois. Alors, comment la France se situe-t-elle par rapport à ses voisins européens ? Si le scénario d’une faillite n’est pas à l’ordre du jour, pour l’instant, aucun signe d’amélioration ne se dessine.

france24fr.title: Crise du logement en Espagne : les mesures de Sánchez jugées insuffisantes
france24fr.description: En Espagne, la mobilisation contre la crise du logement se poursuit, après l’expulsion de Maricarmen, une femme de 87 ans devenue le symbole de la crise à Madrid. Pour tenter d’apaiser la colère, le gouvernement de Pedro Sánchez propose notamment de prolonger jusqu’en 2030 la protection contre les expulsions pour les locataires vulnérables et de renouveler automatiquement certains contrats de location. Mais les manifestants jugent ces mesures insuffisantes et réclament des changements plus struc

france24fr.title: France-Espagne : Macron en visite d’État à Madrid pour resserrer les liens
france24fr.description: Emmanuel Macron et Brigitte Macron sont reçus en grande pompe à Madrid pour une visite d’État de deux jours, la première d’un président français en Espagne depuis 2009. Au-delà du rapprochement politique et européen, cette visite intervient alors que les rapports économiques entre les deux pays ont évolué : l’Espagne affiche une croissance plus forte et un déficit public inférieur à celui de la France, même si elle reste confrontée à un chômage plus élevé et à un PIB par habitant inférieur.

france24fr.title: Javier Milei en opération séduction à Paris
france24fr.description: Le président argentin Javier Milei est à Paris pour défendre son bilan et attirer les investisseurs européens. Si sa thérapie de choc a permis de faire chuter l'inflation et de rétablir les comptes publics, la reprise économique s'essouffle et la pauvreté repart à la hausse.

france24fr.title: Julien Aubert (LR) : les propos antisémites attribués à J. Bardella sont "un risque" pour M. Le Pen
france24fr.description: Julien Aubert, vice-président des Républicains et président d'Osez la France réagit aux accusations d'antisémitisme portées par Mediapart à l'encontre de Jordan Bardella, président du Rassemblement national. Il pense que "ces accusations viennent de l'intérieur" du parti et estime que si celles-ci sont avérées, "le risque pour Marine Le Pen, c'est d'être jugée co-responsable". Il est aussi question du projet présidentiel de Bruno Retailleau, candidat LR, à l'heure où le gouvernement doit présent

france24fr.title: Éliminatoires de la CAN 2027 : première victoire pour Patrick Vieira et le Sénégal
france24fr.description: Patrick Vieira a remporté mardi son premier match en tant que sélectionneur du Sénégal. Les Lions de la Teranga ont gagné sur la pelouse de l’Éthiopie (1-0) grâce à un but d'Ibrahim Mbaye.

france24fr.title: Pollution à l'ozone : plus d'un tiers de la population mondiale dangereusement exposée en 2026
france24fr.description: Plus d'un tiers (34 %) de la population mondiale a été exposé cette année à des niveaux extrêmement élevés de pollution à l'ozone, du fait des vagues de chaleur et des incendies de forêt conjugués aux émissions d'origine humaine, selon un rapport du service européen Copernicus.

france24fr.title: Le RN face aux révélations sur Jordan Bardella : "Dinguerie", "barbouzerie", "manip"
france24fr.description: À la Une de la presse : une manifestation d'étudiants contre le régime iranien à Téhéran, malgré la répression en cours ; la désignation de Fatima Ezzahra El Mansouri au poste de Première ministre du Maroc après la victoire de son parti aux législatives ; l'onde de choc, en France, après les révélations sur des propos antisémites attribués à Jordan Bardella ; et la lecture du roman anglais "Jane Eyre" au programme des écoliers chinois.

france24fr.title: En direct : plusieurs morts lors d'une nouvelle série de frappes russes sur Kiev et ses environs
france24fr.description: Selon des responsables ukrainiens, des frappes ​russes ont fait, tôt ​mercredi, trois morts, dont un ​enfant, et sept blessés à Kiev et dans ses alentours. Une personne a été tuée et une autre blessée lors d'attaques de drones dans la région russe de Briansk, qui borde l'Ukraine, a déclaré le gouverneur Egor Kovalchuk sur l'application de messagerie Telegram. Suivez notre direct.

france24fr.title: Visite de Javier Milei à Paris : "Il n’y a plus d'argent en Argentine, il doit en trouver ailleurs"
france24fr.description: À Paris à partir de mercredi pour un forum économique, Javier Milei cherche de nouveaux investisseurs pour l’Argentine, alors que la croissance reste fragile et que la pauvreté repart à la hausse. Pour le chercheur Jean-Jacques Kourliandsky, le président d’extrême droite argentin vient surtout "pousser des portes qui lui restent encore ouvertes en Europe".

france24fr.title: Irak : la coalition antijihadiste menée par les États-Unis achève son retrait
france24fr.description: Le départ d'Irak des dernières troupes de la coalition anti-État islamique menée par les États-Unis, prévu ce mercredi, met fin à une présence entamée en 2014. Ce retrait relance la question du désarmement des factions pro-iraniennes, dont plusieurs groupes refusent toujours de rendre les armes.

france24fr.title: Après des explosions dans la zone démilitarisée, la Corée du Sud exige des excuses de Pyongyang
france24fr.description: La Corée du Sud exige que son voisin du Nord s'excuse après que des explosions de mines ont blessé trois de ses soldats dans la zone démilitarisée (DMZ) la semaine dernière. Kim Yo-jong, la puissante soeur du dirigeant nord-coréen Kim Jong-un, a rejeté mercredi toute responsabilité et accuse Séoul de fabriquer un prétexte à une "provocation" militaire.

zeit.title: Gasspeicher in Deutschland: Katherina Reiche weist Energieunternehmen zu Gasspeicherung an
zeit.description: Die Bundeswirtschaftsministerin fordert das staatliche Energieunternehmen Sefe auf, Gas einzukaufen und zu speichern. Die Preise sind durch den Irankrieg hoch.

zeit.title: Gasspeicher in Deutschland: Katherina Reiche weist Energieunternehmen zu Gasspeicherung an
zeit.description: Die Bundeswirtschaftsministerin fordert das staatliche Energieunternehmen Sefe auf, Gas einzukaufen und zu speichern. Die Preise sind durch den Irankrieg hoch.

zeit.title: Keks wieder da: Happy-End bei Lama-Suche: Wie kurios die Einfangaktion war
Wohnungslosigkeit: Kältehilfe stellt rund 1.000 Plätze zur Verfügung
Ursache noch unklar: Nach Fassadensturz - Haus vorerst unbewohnbar
Verbraucherpreise: Inflation erstmals seit Dezember 2024 wieder über 3 Prozent
Teurer Alltag: Inflation in NRW ist so hoch wie seit 2023 nicht mehr
Pflegeversicherung: Kabinett beschließt Pflegereform
zeit.description: Union und SPD haben den Streit um die Pflege beigelegt und sich nach ZEIT-Informationen auf ein Stabilisierungspaket geeinigt. Eine strukturelle Reform soll folgen.

zeit.title: Kabinett: Härtere Strafen für Angriffe auf Zugbegleiter und Ärzte
Kriminalität: Viele Drogen bei Durchsuchungen in Halle gefunden
Kampf gegen Rechtsextremismus: Internationaler Polizeieinsatz gegen Nazi-Musik
Joshua Kimmich: Das Kimmich-Dilemma
zeit.description: Deutschland hat nicht mehr so viele Fußballer mit internationalem Renommee. Joshua Kimmich ist einer von ihnen. Dennoch kann er für Jürgen Klopp zum Problem werden.

zeit.title: Binnenschifffahrt: Bitte nur halb vollmachen, sonst läuft der Kahn auf Grund
zeit.description: Die Pegelstände des Rheins sind weiterhin sehr niedrig. Das trifft die Binnenschiffer, treibt die Preise und bremst die Wirtschaft. Ein Besuch an Bord der Nepomuk

zeit.title: Studentenwohnreport 2026: Mieten von Studierenden weiter angestiegen
zeit.description: Studentisches Wohnen wird deutschlandweit teurer. Studierende zahlten laut einer Auswertung im ersten Halbjahr 2026 um 2,6 Prozent mehr Miete als im Jahr zuvor.

zeit.title: Luftverkehr: Passagierflugzeug setzt auf dem Weg nach Tel Aviv Notfallsignal ab
zeit.description: Eine Maschine mit 180 Menschen an Bord ist in Saudi-Arabien notgelandet. Grund war wohl ein Streit zwischen den Piloten, die Berichte darüber sind jedoch widersprüchlich.

nzz.title: LIVE-TICKER - Krieg in der Ukraine: Russland droht Nato mit Atomwaffeneinsatz bei Blockade Kaliningrads
nzz.description: Seit über vier Jahren führt Russland Krieg gegen die Ukraine. Die wichtigsten Entwicklungen im Überblick.

nzz.title: Deutsche Regierung bringt Pflegereform auf den Weg
nzz.description: Bis kurz vor dem geplanten Kabinettstermin ringen Union und SPD um einen Kompromiss in ihrem Streit um die Pflege. Dann gibt es grünes Licht für die Reform.

nzz.title: KOMMENTAR - Der Ständerat verliert in der EU-Debatte den Blick aufs Ganze
nzz.description: Bei der Europadebatte im Parlament sind Befürworter der EU-Verträge mit angezogener Handbremse unterwegs. Die Gegner setzen auf Untergangsrhetorik und drücken sich davor, eine realistische Alternative zum Bilateralismus zu benennen.

nzz.title: FBI wird gehackt – Cyberkriminelle entwenden heikle Personaldaten und Informationen zu Geheimaufträgen
nzz.description: Die Hackergruppe Shiny Hunters hat schon manchen spektakulären Coup ausgeführt. Jetzt hat sie persönliche Daten von Tausenden von FBI-Agenten gestohlen. Für die amerikanische Bundespolizei ist es ein Debakel – und ein beträchtliches Sicherheitsrisiko.

nzz.title: Flugzeug nach Tel Aviv muss in Saudiarabien notlanden: Wollte ein Pilot die Maschine abstürzen lassen?
nzz.description: Ein Notruf aus einer Flydubai-Maschine auf dem Weg nach Tel Aviv hat am Mittwochmorgen israelische Kampfjets auf den Plan gerufen. Das Flugzeug landete im saudiarabischen Tabuk.

nzz.title: Greta Thunberg in Zürich: «Ein Betrug auf so vielen Ebenen»
nzz.description: Die Klima- und Palästina-Aktivistin macht sich nun für das Volk der Sahraouis in der Westsahara stark. Auch am Zurich Film Festival. Was steckt dahinter?

nzz.title: MELDUNGEN WIRTSCHAFT - China droht EU mit Gegenmassnahmen im Handelsstreit
LIVE-TICKER - Iran-Krieg: Zwei Männer nach Massenprotesten in Iran hingerichtet
nzz.description: Die USA und Iran befinden sich seit Februar 2026 im Kriegszustand. Zwar haben die beiden Länder eine Waffenruhe vereinbart, doch Donald Trump hat diese Anfang Juli für beendet erklärt. Die neuesten Entwicklungen im Ticker.

nzz.title: INTERVIEW - «Wenn die Schweiz nur noch Luxusuhren macht, reicht das wahrscheinlich nicht»
nzz.description: Die Schweizer Uhrenindustrie exportiert immer weniger Uhren. Die auf Luxusgüter spezialisierte Deloitte-Partnerin Karine Szegedi erklärt, warum das für Zulieferer zum Problem wird – und warum «Swiss made» allein nicht mehr genügt.

nzz.title: PODCAST «NZZ GEOPOLITIK» - Politisch unter Druck der USA, wirtschaftlich abhängig von China: Bei den Wahlen steht Brasiliens Blockfreiheit auf dem Spiel
nzz.description: Am 4. Oktober wird in Brasilien ein neues Staatsoberhaupt gewählt. Im Duell zwischen Amtsinhaber Lula und seinem stärksten Herausforderer, Flavio Bolsonaro, geht es auch um die Frage, wie Brasilien sich geopolitisch positioniert in einer zunehmend bipolaren Welt zwischen Washington und Peking.

nzz.title: Die Rohölexporte aus den Golfstaaten steigen leicht – doch neue Risiken sind schon in Sicht
nzz.description: Die Golfstaaten exportierten im September mehr Rohöl als in den Vormonaten. Nachhaltig ist die Situation allerdings nicht.

nzz.title: Österreichs Sozialdemokratie in der Krise: Ein TV-Millionär kämpft um die SPÖ-Krone
nzz.description: Gerhard Zeiler, 71, international erfolgreicher Manager bei Warner Bros., fordert Österreichs Vizekanzler Andreas Babler als SPÖ-Vorsitzenden heraus. Die einst staatstragende Partei ist in Umfragen auf 15 Prozent abgestürzt und weiss nicht, wohin und mit wem.

nzz.title: Teures Gas und Erdöl: Die EU bereitet sich auf einen «sehr harten Winter» vor, sagt der EU-Kommissar
nzz.description: Europa gerät finanziell unter Druck. Die Gasspeicher müssen für viel Geld weiter gefüllt werden. Die Konsumenten werden es spüren, weil für Entlastungsmassnahmen fehlt zunehmend das Geld. Es rächen sich die Versäumnisse im Frühjahr.

nzz.title: KOMMENTAR - Die Schweiz ist das letzte Nullzinsland: Doch das sich ändernde Umfeld bietet der SNB die Chance für einen Zinsschritt
nzz.description: In der ganzen Welt gibt es positive nominale Zinsen – ausser in der Schweiz. Das hat gute Gründe, doch in den vergangenen Monaten hat sich die Ausgangslage für die Schweizerische Nationalbank verändert.

observador.title: Alvaiázere prepara 22.ª edição do Festival do Chícharo
observador.description: Festival gastronómico arranca sexta-feira, voltando a colocar em destaque os produtos endógenos da região. Evento inclui ainda concertos de Bárbara Tinoco e Xutos & Pontapés.

observador.title: Luana do Bem: "As pessoas passam-se mesmo nas redes sociais"
observador.description: Luana do Bem defende o teste de piadas nos palcos como a chave do sucesso na comédia. A humorista critica a extrema toxicidade nas redes sociais que contrasta com o respeito sentido num espetáculo.

observador.title: Um terço dos portugueses estão descontentes com cidades
observador.description: Inquérito revela que as cidades portuguesas apresentam resultados menos favoráveis do que os registados no resto da Europa. Na Área Metropolitana de Lisboa apenas 58% dos residentes estão satisfeitos.

observador.title: Mercado Time Out exige 615 mil euros à Metro do Porto
observador.description: Mercado Time Out exige que lhe sejam pagos pela Metro do Porto 615 mil euros, divididos entre despesas extraordinárias, lucros cessantes e danos de imagem e reputacionais.

observador.title: ProfJam faz "viagem sem fronteiras" no Coliseu de Lisboa
observador.description: Das canções nunca esquecidas, "às que esses palcos maiores não ouvem há demasiado tempo", até às que estão por ouvir, o rapper português anuncia concerto em que vai viajar por toda a sua obra.

observador.title: Investimento em retalho destaca-se em Portugal
observador.description: O retalho continua em expansão, com os centros comerciais a surgirem como grandes protagonistas do investimento imobiliário, num setor onde os consumidores tendem a privilegiar a experiência.

observador.title: Debater corrupção nas escolas combate descrença na politica?
observador.description: Mouraz Lopes salienta a importância de criar nas escolas uma cultura de integração dos jovens afastados de atos de corrupção. Alexandre Homem Cristo aponta para o combate à cultura de ganho rápido.

observador.title: Mais de 1.900 detidos e meia tonelada de droga apreendida
observador.description: PSP anunciou ter feito 5.558 apreensões entre janeiro e julho, num total de mais de 380 quilos de canábis, quase 100 quilos de cocaína, mais de 25 quilos de heroína e 5.500 unidades de ecstasy.

observador.title: 10h. Arrancou a campanha de vacinação contra a gripe
observador.description: Dura até 31 de março do próximo ano nos centros de saúde e em farmácias de todo o país. Ainda, o PM britânico não descarta a possibilidade de o Reino Unido voltar à União Europeia.

observador.title: A relação entre o PSD e o Chega atingiu o limite?
observador.description: Será que o Governo se aproximou do PS para aprovar o Orçamento de Estado? E o Chega, estará a ser pressionado à sua direita?

observador.title: Burnham abre a porta ao regresso à UE e critica Brexit
observador.description: Andy Burnham foi mais longe do que Starmer e admitiu publicamente que o Reino Unido pode regressar à UE, sublinhando que "cerca de 60% dos britânicos" apoiam essa ideia.

observador.title: Montenegro dá aula sobre ética e integridade em escola
observador.description: O combate à corrupção deve começar no "espaço onde se aprende a cidadania". "É diferente ouvir o primeiro-ministro ou ouvir o diretor da Polícia Judiciária", diz secretário de Estado da Educação.

observador.title: 9h. Avião que ia do Dubai até Israel aterra de emergência
observador.description: Há suspeitas de sequestro, desvio ou interferência ilegal. Ainda, Parlamento debate nova lei do arrendamento, mas tem chumbo à vista.

observador.title: Delcy Rodríguez reconhece "uso abusivo" de lei contra o ódio
observador.description: Ao longo da última década, dezenas de responsáveis políticos, ativistas, jornalistas, manifestantes e influenciadores foram acusados de "incitamento ao ódio" e detidos com base nesta lei, de 2017.

observador.title: Quase 40% da população mundial exposta a poluição perigosa
observador.description: Zona mais atingida foi a Ásia, seguindo-se a Europa e depois a América do Norte, com grande parte do hemisfério norte com valores acima da meta recomendada pela Organização Mundial de Saúde (OMS).

observador.title: Supremo rejeita ação contra decreto sobre venda de terras
observador.description: Decreto assinado por Milei em dezembro de 2023 estabeleceu uma extensa série de reformas ao sistema jurídico argentino em múltiplos aspetos e gerou um grande número de impugnações nos tribunais.

observador.title: Mais de metade do crédito à habitação tem intermediários
observador.description: Estudo comparativo analisou 10 países e concluiu que Portugal foi o quarto entre os 10 analisados em que a intermediação de crédito tem maior peso na distribuição de crédito à habitação, com 57%.

observador.title: Oceanos têm aquecido a "ritmo alarmante"
observador.description: Com o aquecimento dos oceanos surgem ondas de calor marinhas e intensificam-se tempestades, perturbando os ecossistemas e contribuindo para a elevação do nível do mar.

spiegel.title: Brasilien: So schreien die lautesten Vögel der Welt
spiegel.description: Forscher haben in den USA und Brasilien 123 Vogelschreie aufgezeichnet – darunter zwei, die etwa so laut sind wie ein Presslufthammer. Hier können Sie sich den Rotfußseriema und den Nacktgesichtkotinga anhören.

spiegel.title: Iran: Armee setzt Kopfgeld auf getötete US-Soldaten aus
spiegel.description: Iran will Bürgerinnen und Bürger belohnen, die US-Soldaten töten oder gefangen nehmen. Frauen sollen dabei die doppelte Prämie erhalten.

spiegel.title: Hohe Preise: Tankstellen klagen über Betrug an Zapfsäulen
spiegel.description: Weil Benzin und Sprit derzeit so teuer sind, verzichten offenbar manche Autofahrer darauf, für ihre Tankfüllung zu bezahlen. Erste Tankstellenbetreiber reagieren bereits.

spiegel.title: Bayern: Seniorin übergibt nach Schockanruf fast halbe Million Euro an Betrüger
spiegel.description: In Germering ist eine mehr als 70 Jahre alte Frau auf Betrüger hereingefallen. Ein angeblicher Polizist hatte zuvor am Telefon Druck aufgebaut und eine hohe Summe von der Seniorin verlangt.

spiegel.title: Bundesregierung: Kabinett beschließt Pflegereform
spiegel.description: Die Bundesregierung gibt nach langem Ringen von Union und SPD grünes Licht für die geplante Pflegereform. Das Kabinett beschließt den Gesetzentwurf von Gesundheitsminister Linnemann zur Neuordnung der Pflegeversicherung.

spiegel.title: Nordkorea: Kim Jong Un ist laut Südkoreas Geheimdienst »extrem fettleibig«
spiegel.description: Nordkoreas Machthaber Kim wiegt laut südkoreanischem Geheimdienst 140 Kilogramm. Er soll eine Vorliebe für teure Speisen haben. In seinem Land sieht die Uno Nahrungsmittelknappheit als großes humanitäres Problem an.

spiegel.title: İlkay Gündoğan musste über ein Jahr auf diese Medaille warten
spiegel.description: Es ist bei Weitem nicht der erste Preis für İlkay Gündoğan. Aber diese Auszeichnung ist eine besondere. Um sie ihm endlich zu überreichen, brauchte es eine Türkeireise von NRW-Ministerpräsident Hendrik Wüst.

spiegel.title: »EA Sports FC 27«: Trainerinnen in Unterwäsche – Update soll Fehler beseitigen
spiegel.description: Seit einigen Jahren enthält »EA Sports FC«, das früher »Fifa« hieß, neben Männerfußball auch Trainer- und Fußballerinnen. Die neueste Version des Spiels macht jetzt mit einem »Bikini-Bug« Schlagzeilen.

spiegel.title: Budapest: Berufungsgericht reduziert Haftstrafe für Maja T. auf sieben Jahre
spiegel.description: Wegen Angriffen auf Rechtsextreme in Ungarn wurde Maja T. verurteilt. Nun erzielt die non-binäre Person einen Erfolg. Das Berufungsgericht wertete T. nicht als Mitglied einer kriminellen Vereinigung und reduzierte die Strafe.

spiegel.title: Ärzteblatt-Umfrage: Kinder und Jugendliche greifen vermehrt zu Energydrinks
spiegel.description: Junge Menschen trinken häufiger koffeinhaltige Energydrinks. Experten warnen vor gesundheitlichen Folgen – und bringen das Konsumverhalten mit sozialer Herkunft in Verbindung.

spiegel.title: Reformpolitik: Warum die Regierung vor der Mitte einknickt
spiegel.description: Die schwarz-rote Koalition habe ein falsches Verständnis von Reformpolitik und knicke zu schnell vor der Mittelschicht ein, sagt der Sozialethiker Bernhard Emunds. Er sieht für Merz aber auch einen Ausweg.

spiegel.title: Israel – Saudi-Arabien: Piloten prügeln sich auf Linienflug von Dubai nach Tel Aviv
spiegel.description: Der Flug einer Passagiermaschine von Dubai nach Tel Aviv endete mit einer Notlandung in Saudi-Arabien. An Bord sollen die Piloten aufeinander losgegangen sein. Zunächst bestand sogar die Sorge vor einer Entführung.

spiegel.title: Südkorea: Verirrter Bullenhai wird zum Star
spiegel.description: Die Koreaner haben einen dreieinhalb Meter langen Hai ins Herz geschlossen. Das Tier sitzt seit zwei Wochen in einem Kanal in Busan fest. Es kurbelt den Eisabsatz an – und lässt sogar Börsenkurse steigen.

spiegel.title: Bundesagentur für Arbeit: Zahl der Arbeitslosen bleibt im September auf hohem Niveau

phys-org.title: One-third of world population exposed to harmful air pollution: Monitor
phys-org.description: Heat waves and wildfires combined with human-caused emissions this year to expose one-third of the world's population to extremely high levels of ozone pollution, a European Union report said Wednesday.

phys-org.title: Paw-fect candidate: Australia finds new koala rescue dog
phys-org.description: The hunt is over: After trawling through dozens of applications, an Australian animal welfare group has found a successor to a hero hound credited with saving more than 100 koalas from fires.

phys-org.title: Insects are essential to vertebrate life—as food, shelter and medicine
phys-org.description: While insects provide an essential food source for many vertebrate species, they're more than just a protein-laden snack. Chimpanzees use them to sterilize wounds, and herons use them as fishing bait. Sloths rely on moths to maintain the algae in their fur, which they then eat. Birds and reptiles lay their eggs inside the temperature-controlled sanctuary of termite mounds, while some desert frogs reside in ant nests because of the humidity.

phys-org.title: Dinosaur snacked on seaweed washed up on North American coasts, fossil teeth suggest
phys-org.description: Storms routinely wash marine material ashore, providing food for land animals and other organisms. This is known as marine subsidization (MS). Today, MS is particularly common in coastal ecosystems and is especially important to animals when land ecosystems produce less food than usual, such as during droughts. A new Frontiers in Ecology and Evolution study has shown that dinos and their prey, too, may have eaten seafood washed onto beaches.

phys-org.title: Crystal spacing predicts magnetic states in complex alloys better than electron count
phys-org.description: In materials chemistry, identifying common parameters that can organize magnetic ground states across complex intermetallic compounds remains a central challenge. Researchers have long used chemically tunable parameters to control magnetic properties. One is valence-electron concentration, commonly discussed as the electron-per-atom (e/a) ratio. The e/a ratio has been widely used to classify magnetic ground states in metallic systems such as Heusler alloys and approximant crystals.

phys-org.title: Camera system sheds new light on bird collisions at sea
phys-org.description: Research into bird collisions with offshore wind turbines has taken an important step forward. A yearlong pilot study at an offshore wind turbine has shown that thermal cameras and artificial intelligence can be used to directly observe potential collisions at sea. The technology proved effective under challenging conditions while also generating rare real-world data on bird movements around a wind turbine.

phys-org.title: Unlocking AI as a research tool for plant microscopy
phys-org.description: Software created by University of Queensland scientists could help AI platforms overcome a blind spot limiting their value in plant research. UQ Ph.D. student Tianqi Wei said even advanced vision-language models (VLMs) had difficulty interpreting images of microscopic plant details.

phys-org.title: Small fields, great diversity: How a diverse patchwork of crops helps birds
phys-org.description: Birds are not only beautiful to look at and listen to; they also play important roles in nature. They eat pests and disperse seeds. They are generally considered indicators of a healthy environment. When birds thrive, soil and water quality often benefit as well. A new study published in the journal Landscape Ecology shows that growing a variety of crops in small field patches creates better habitats for birds.

phys-org.title: Engineered coating lets mitochondria retain their ability to produce energy
phys-org.description: Researchers have coated mitochondria with innovative materials without compromising their function, according to a study by IRCCS Fondazione Istituto Neurologico Carlo Besta (FINCB) and Politecnico di Milano. The research was conducted as part of the BraiNs joint laboratory, inaugurated in 2023.

phys-org.title: NYC delivery workers injured at more than five times national rate under intense labor control by apps, survey finds
phys-org.description: More than half of New York City's app-based food delivery workers have been injured on the job, and 40% meet the criteria for severe psychological distress, according to a new study from the CUNY Graduate School of Public Health and Health Policy (CUNY SPH), in partnership with the Worker's Justice Project (WJP).

phys-org.title: Beyond temperature: How people experience urban heat
phys-org.description: Urban heat is more than a matter of temperature. It can affect how people sleep, work, travel through the city and dress, and even how safe or comfortable they feel in public spaces. Yet these everyday consequences often remain invisible in conventional assessments of urban heat.

phys-org.title: Alien life? Why the possibility of exoplanet LHS 1140b emitting helium gas is so exciting
phys-org.description: This summer, exoplanet science—the study of planets orbiting stars beyond our sun—took a big step forward. Reports of helium gas escaping from the atmosphere of LHS 1140b propelled this exoplanet from the pages of scientific journals into the mainstream media.

phys-org.title: Nine generations of virtual dating reveal how fish shape their ideal mates
phys-org.description: Fish have "designed" their perfect partners in a new experiment—revealing simple male preferences and more complex female tastes.

phys-org.title: Revisiting a Young Isaac Newton
phys-org.description: Isaac Newton is typically portrayed as a solitary scientist with intense focus who was obsessed with power and deeply egotistical. But a new book by Caltech historians Jed Buchwald and Mordechai Feingold takes a deeper look at Newton's life in the two decades leading up to the 1687 publication of his groundbreaking text, Principia Mathematica, when he was 44. Using newly digitized scans of Newton's early writings, Buchwald and Feingold uncover a portrait of the young polymath as a curi

phys-org.title: Why monkeys handle conflicts better than we do
phys-org.description: Conflicts with our colleagues, loved ones or team members can quickly stifle communication, heighten tensions and undermine relationships. However, a decision or compromise is not always enough to restore cooperation—for a solution to last, we must also repair the bond that will allow people to continue moving forward together.

phys-org.title: Rethinking liquid hydrogen storage with metal-organic frameworks
phys-org.description: Liquid hydrogen (LH₂) is attractive for long-distance energy transport because of its high volumetric energy density. But even well-insulated tanks cannot completely prevent heat from entering. As the liquid warms, hydrogen evaporates and pressure builds, leading to boil-off losses during storage and transport.

phys-org.title: How a new textile fabric could triple production in strawberry plants
phys-org.description: A new textile used to cover strawberry plants more than tripled fruit yields in tunnel field tests without harming plant health. The technology could also significantly reduce water and pesticide use in strawberry fields.

undark.title: Podcast: Should We Put AI-Enabled Tech in Our Brains?
undark.description: Welcome to Season 3 of Entanglements! In our first episode, we discuss neural implants and AI with Judy Illes, a professor of neurology and neuroethics at the University of British Columbia, and Joseph J. Fins, a physician scientist and medical ethicist at Weill Cornell Medicine in New York.

undark.title: Engineering Animals to Grow Human Organs — But Not Human Minds
undark.description: Chimeras, or animals with human cells and tissues, are not new, and researchers have long used them to gain insights into diseases and even as a potential source of transplantable organs. But the research brings up thorny ethical questions regarding animal rights and the moral status of chimeric creatures.

undark.title: AI-Driven Biology Is Only as Good as the Data Beneath It
undark.description: Opinion | The biotech and pharma industries are pouring billions of dollars into AI-driven drug discovery and development. But the genomic data used to train AI models are often incomplete, contain errors, or lack contextual information — a quality issue that threatens to slow the pace of biological research.

undark.title: In Italy, What Earth Can Tell Us About Extraterrestrial Life
undark.description: Photo Essay | From sampling hydrothermal vents and abandoned mines to lab experiments that replicate Mars’ atmosphere, scientists are using what we know about life on Earth to understand how it may exist on other worlds. Italy, it seems, provides particularly fertile ground for such explorations.

undark.title: The Evolving Quest to Build Life in a Lab
undark.description: Scientists are trying to create new life, whether to understand how biology first developed on Earth, or design new cells from scratch.  But life hasn’t happened — at least not yet. And questions around safety, as well as what even constitutes life in the first place, continue to swirl.

undark.title: The Embryos That Don’t Come From Eggs and Sperm
undark.description: Human embryo models mimic the earliest development stages; they could offer a glimpse of the first weeks of pregnancy — a mysterious period for which natural embryos are seldom available — and potentially shed light on miscarriage, congenital anomalies, and other health issues. But how far should they go?

undark.title: Book Review: A Contrarian View of How Consciousness Evolved
undark.description: In “Natural Intelligence & the Logic of Consciousness,” neuroscientist Antonio Damasio argues against the conventional theory that consciousness stems from high-level brain function and cognition, which in turn leads to feelings. Instead, he writes, our basest feelings led us to our loftiest thoughts.

undark.title: AI Presents Science with a ‘Ship of Theseus’ Problem
undark.description: Opinion | AI is being integrated into every part of the scientific process, including education, publishing, and the research itself. What does it mean if every component of the enterprise gets replaced by AI tools over time? C. Brandon Ogbunu explores what happens when science gets stripped of human involvement.

undark.title: Interview: What Does the ‘I’ in AI Really Mean?
undark.description: Is it possible that AI is — or might one day become — truly intelligent? Undark posed the question to five experts in linguistics, computer science, cognitive science, and psychology. They offered very different answers, though they agreed that the term “intelligence” is vague and poorly suited to the debate.

undark.title: Book Excerpt: Why the Brain Isn’t the Self
undark.description: The brain isn’t the self — consciousness is intimately linked with the human body. And if consciousness is the body’s way of knowing itself, then it is the living form in its entirety that should be taken as selfhood proper, with the brain as an especially feverish region.

proj-syn.title: Investing in Brain Health
proj-syn.description: Just as AI agents are mastering complex cognitive tasks, our own ability to perform the same tasks is eroding. Whether AI vindicates its boosters or fizzles out like the Metaverse craze of 2022, we will not fare well without a civilization-wide effort to rebuild the cognitive skills that make technological progress possible.

proj-syn.title: Europe Still Needs Molecules
proj-syn.description: Not even the most effective European electrification strategy will eliminate the need for the molecules that fossil fuels provide. Given this, Europe must diversify its oil and gas supplies, maintain its refining capacity, and lock in decarbonization by building a hydrogen-energy industry at scale.

proj-syn.title: Energy Security in an Age of Disruption
proj-syn.description: While there is no single prescription for energy security, strengthening “response capacity,” such as by establishing stockpiles, substituting sources, and diversifying suppliers, is essential. The point is not to eliminate vulnerabilities altogether, but to ensure that there are options when disruption arrives.

proj-syn.title: Africa’s Common Currency-in-Waiting
proj-syn.description: While the phased approach of the Economic Community of West African States to implementing a long-delayed single currency will maintain momentum without compromising macroeconomic discipline, the bloc still lacks a robust mechanism to address asymmetric shocks. That is why fiscal integration must come first.

proj-syn.title: Learning to Reconcile
proj-syn.description: Political discourse in many Western countries has broken down, making it difficult for people with different viewpoints to live amicably with one another. The Reconciliation League, an international initiative by 13 universities and colleges, aims to train a generation of leaders who can change that.

proj-syn.title: Sheinbaum Is Just Another Trump Appeaser
proj-syn.description: After two years in office, Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum continues to be widely praised, both in Mexico and abroad, for her handling of US President Donald Trump. But Sheinbaum has skillfully—and cynically—disguised the extent to which she has deferred to Trump on almost every issue.

proj-syn.title: Distorted Intelligence at the AI Frontier
proj-syn.description: The real problem for the frontier AI labs is not that their models are too powerful and already “misaligned” with the goals their creators set for them. Rather, it is that the models are being trained in ways that may be leading to a type of intelligence that will become less predictable.

proj-syn.title: Good Growth Requires the Right Public Finance
proj-syn.description: Although the Labour Party has done more to strengthen the United Kingdom's public-finance ecosystem in the past two years than any government in a generation, it must not stop there. If public investment is to meet its full potential, it must be reorganized to operate at scale on the public's behalf.

proj-syn.title: An EU–Canada Partnership Against Coercion
proj-syn.description: By proposing that the European Union and Canada begin work toward an association agreement, European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen has taken a critical first step toward establishing Europe as a hub for the world’s democratic middle powers. Such an arrange

proj-syn.title: The Opposing Forces Reshaping Global Finance
proj-syn.description: The financial industry is being pulled between two powerful forces: bottom-up financial technology is enabling seamless integration, while top-down geoeconomic statecraft is promoting fragmentation. So much for the conventional wisdom that finance will simply become smoother, cheaper, and more globalized over time.

proj-syn.title: The Dismally Obedient Science
proj-syn.description: While empirical inquiry has its place in economics, the pursuit of causality must not be allowed to displace the pursuit of explanation. Beyond identifying causal effects within existing arrangements, economists must investigate how those arrangements are produced, reproduced, and contested.

proj-syn.title: Oligarchy Is a Symptom, Not a Cause
proj-syn.description: The deepening political dysfunction plaguing the US can be traced not to wealth inequality, as some argue, but to the fact that different groups of voters believe different facts. A political strategy that takes this into account might eventually lead to wealth redistribution, but it must begin with improved critical-thinking skills.

proj-syn.title: The Immigrants Leading the Anti-Immigrant Far Right
proj-syn.description: Right-wing populists have turned hypocrisy into a successful electoral strategy. But those voting for nativism in Europe and the United States should be careful what they wish for: They may end up expelling their own family members, if not their own political leaders.

proj-syn.title: The Great AI Gamble
proj-syn.description: As the two world leaders in AI development and adoption, the United States and China are each operating under assumptions that justify ever-faster progress, regardless of the risks. The current thinking is not unlike the rationale once given for Stalinist brutality in the name of rapid modernization.

proj-syn.title: The Un-Ordered UN Order
proj-syn.description: As European leaders hobnob with their counterparts at the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly, they must think carefully about how to navigate a fast-changing multilateral landscape. The old world belonged to rule-makers and institution-builders, but the current one favors those who can improvise.

proj-syn.title: AI Needs Trusted Journalism
proj-syn.description: As people increasingly rely on AI chatbots for news, the already tenuous bargain between publishers and tech firms—the former invested in journalism that the latter helped audiences discover—is no longer workable. UNESCO’s proposed Guidance on Fair Compensation for News could help create a new value-exchange model.

proj-syn.title: How to Stop the AI-pocalypse
proj-syn.description: AI could very well end democracy, if not humanity, yet efforts to slow its development may fail as companies and countries race to stay ahead. Preventing such a future will require international coordination and taxing the extreme wealth that could put unprecedented power in the hands of a tiny elite.

proj-syn.title: What Killed Liberalism?
proj-syn.description: There is no shortage of people and ideas to blame for liberalism’s decline, but searching for a single culprit is probably futile. Two new books by Gordon Brown and Daron Acemoglu take up the harder question of how to rebuild the institutions that once gave people a sense of community and power over their lives.
